alt: Editorial plate: a floodlit night at Anfield, a midfielder in red striking a volley from thirty yards, the ball leaving his boot in a blur, a goalkeeper in the distance beginning to move the wrong way, a wall of supporters rising behind the goal.
focus: Carried plate, not this edition's lead. The Szoboszlai volley from Liverpool 3-1 Tottenham, Carabao Cup third round, 15 September, remains the season's most recent photographable moment while the front page leads on matchday itself: Bournemouth away, Andoni Iraola's first return to the club he managed, and the game in hand paid at two o'clock.
leadStory: It is matchday, Sunday 20 September. Liverpool play Bournemouth away at 2pm at the Vitality Stadium, the last fixture of the round and Andoni Iraola's first return to the club he managed for three years and left in June. The game in hand that dropped Liverpool to tenth on Saturday, when five results moved the table around a club that did not play, is finally paid. The one live team-news question is Cody Gakpo, the most productive Liverpool forward of the autumn, who did not train on Saturday with soreness in both adductors and whom Iraola would not guarantee, 'I cannot guarantee it', per This Is Anfield, with Rio Ngumoha the ready replacement on the left. Otherwise Iraola reported no fresh problems out of the cup, with Bradley, Chiesa, Ekitike and Leoni the four long-term out, and the rested seniors, Alisson, Van Dijk, Isak, Wirtz and Barcola, restored to the league XI. Bournemouth are sixteenth and winless, the only side in Premier League history to lead each of its opening four fixtures and win none, fresh from the first European win in their history at Real Sociedad on Thursday.
